summary: Use a Merchant Profile at the top of a payment to show who is being paid: the merchant’s logo, registered name, and UPI ID.

useWhen.text: At the top of a payment, to show who is being paid: the merchant's logo, registered name, and UPI ID.

from.quote: Use a Merchant Profile at the top of a payment to show who is being paid: the merchant’s logo, registered name, and UPI ID.

avoidWhen.text: A merchant header that people press: the profile has no states and doesn't press.

from.quote: The profile has no states: it doesn’t press.

anatomy.holds: avatarProps: the merchant's logo, or initials with style Monogram.

from.quote: avatarProps: the merchant’s logo, or initials with style Monogram.

anatomy.holds: title: the registered name, 16 px Bold; it wraps.

from.quote: title: the registered name, 16 px Bold; it wraps.

anatomy.holds: subtitle, 12 px under the name; it wraps too.

from.quote: subtitle, 12 px under the name; it wraps too.

placementAdvice.text: A payment screen opens with the merchant, so people know who they're paying before they enter the amount.

from.quote: A payment screen opens with the merchant, so people know who they’re paying before they enter the amount.

placementAdvice.text: Who you're paying, before how much.

from.quote: Who you’re paying, before how much.

placementAdvice.text: The screen lays out the rest and sends the payment; the profile shows who is being paid.

from.quote: The screen lays out the rest and sends the payment.

placementAdvice.text: The profile has no width of its own: it fills its column, keeps 16 px clear at each side, and centres its lines. Figma draws it 360 px wide.

from.quote: The profile has no width of its own: it fills its column, keeps 16 px clear at each side, and centres its lines; Figma draws it 360 px wide.

placementAdvice.text: In a stretching column it fills the width; in a centring one it hugs its content.

from.quote: In a stretching column it fills the width; in a centring one it hugs its content.

placementAdvice.text: With a one-line name it's 102 px tall: a 42 px avatar, 12 px, a 20 px name, 12 px, and a 16 px UPI ID.

from.quote: With a one-line name it’s 102 px tall: a 42 px avatar, 12 px, a 20 px name, 12 px, and a 16 px UPI ID.

configuration.text: avatarProps goes to the Avatar: an imageSource for the merchant's logo, or style Monogram with their initials.

from.quote: avatarProps goes to the Avatar: an imageSource for the merchant’s logo, or style Monogram with their initials.

configuration.text: Pass the merchant's logo, or their initials.

from.quote: Pass the merchant’s logo, or their initials.

configuration.text: For initials, use style Monogram with the merchant’s initials.

from.quote: or style Monogram with their initials.

configuration.text: Don't leave avatarProps out: the Avatar falls back to a stranger's photo.

from.quote: The Avatar falls back to a stranger’s photo.

configuration.text: Avatar Size sets the avatar, 42 px at L; no mode changes the text.

from.quote: Avatar Size sets the avatar, 42 px at L; no mode changes the text.

configuration.text: Avatar Size M gives a 36 px avatar; S gives 29 px.

from.quote: A 36 px avatar; S is 29 px.

configuration.text: Leave title or subtitle out and it shows sample text, so hide the subtitle with an empty one.

from.quote: Leave title or subtitle out and it shows sample text, so hide the subtitle with an empty one.

configuration.text: To show just the name, pass an empty subtitle: it hides the line.

from.quote: An empty subtitle to hide it

configuration.text: Don't leave subtitle out to hide it: it shows the sample UPI ID, uberindia@ybl.

from.quote: It shows the sample UPI ID, uberindia@ybl.

configuration.text: Figma's Title and Subtitle text properties and its nested Avatar are title, subtitle, and avatarProps in the package.

rules.text: Write title as the merchant's registered name, the one their bank holds, so people know who they're paying.

from.quote: Write title as the merchant’s registered name, the one their bank holds, so people know who they’re paying.

rules.text: Use the company's full name, such as Uber India Systems Private Limited.

from.quote: The company’s full name.

rules.text: Start subtitle with “UPI ID:” and give the ID they're paying, so they can check it.

from.quote: Start subtitle with UPI ID: and give the ID they’re paying, so they can check it.

rules.text: Set title yourself: left out, the profile shows “Uber India Systems Private Limited”.
Set subtitle yourself, or pass an empty one to hide the line: left out, it shows “UPI ID: uberindia@ybl”.

states.when: Always: the profile has no states; it doesn't press.

from.quote: The profile has no states: it doesn’t press.

states.when: In a narrow column both lines wrap and stay centred, and neither ends in an ellipsis, though Figma cuts a long UPI ID.

examples.purpose: A payment screen opens with the merchant, the guide’s In context: Jio Gold’s logo, registered name, and UPI ID, so people know who they’re paying before they enter the amount. The screen lays out the rest (in the guide, the amount, a note and a Pay ₹1,200 button) and sends the payment. The URI stands for the merchant’s own logo.
examples.jsx:
<MerchantProfile
  title="Jio Gold"
  subtitle="UPI ID: jiogold@jio"
  avatarProps={{ imageSource: { uri: 'https://example.com/jio-gold-logo.png' } }}
/>

from.quote: A payment screen opens with the merchant, so people know who they’re paying before they enter the amount.

examples.purpose: A merchant shown by initials: style Monogram with two letters.
examples.jsx:
<MerchantProfile
  title="Amazon Pay"
  subtitle="UPI ID: amazonpay@apl"
  avatarProps={{ style: 'Monogram', monogram: 'AP' }}
/>

from.quote: style Monogram with two letters.

examples.purpose: Just the name: an empty subtitle hides the line (left out, it would show the sample UPI ID).
examples.jsx:
<MerchantProfile
  title="Jio Gold"
  subtitle=""
  avatarProps={{ imageSource: { uri: 'https://example.com/jio-gold-logo.png' } }}
/>

from.quote: An empty subtitle hides the line.

props.name: title
props.description: The name: 16 px Bold on a 20 px line (the package raises the token's 18), centred; it wraps. Declared: The merchant's display name or title. Default "Uber India Systems Private Limited", from the component source.

props.name: subtitle
props.description: The UPI ID line: 12 px Medium on a 16 px line, centred; it wraps, with no ellipsis. Declared: Subtitle text, typically the UPI ID or additional merchant info. Default "UPI ID: uberindia@ybl", from the component source.

props.name: modes
props.description: The profile's own 12 tokens have one mode, so no mode changes the text, gap, or padding. Declared: Mode configuration passed to the token resolver. Also passed to the Avatar child component for consistent theming.

props.name: style
props.description: Optional style overrides for the container.

props.name: avatarProps
props.description: Spread onto the Avatar: imageSource (a logo), or style 'Monogram' with monogram. With neither, the Avatar's bundled stock photo of a person shows. Declared: Props to pass to the Avatar component.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Does nothing: the root renders no label. Declared: Accessibility label for the merchant profile region.

modes.name: Avatar Size
modes.description: Modes reach the Avatar: L 42 px (the default), M 36, S 29, XS 14. XS is too small for two initials. Declared: A token collection MerchantProfile reads (the package's FIGMA_COMPONENT_MODES). When modes leave it unset, the resolver uses the collection's default mode.

gaps.text: A left-out title or subtitle shows sample text (Uber India Systems Private Limited, UPI ID: uberindia@ybl) (Component Bug #423).
The Avatar shows a stock photo until you pass a logo or initials in avatarProps (Component Bug #423).
An empty title or subtitle hides the text but keeps its 12 px gap: 86 px tall without a subtitle, 82 without a title (Component Bug #423).
avatarProps.modes replaces the profile's modes on the avatar instead of merging with them (Component Bug #423).
The name's lines are 20 px where Figma's are 18, so a two-line name is 122 px tall where Figma's is 118 (Component Bug #423).
A long UPI ID wraps where Figma cuts it with an ellipsis (Component Bug #423).
The whole profile is a heading: on the web its root is an h1 around the avatar and both lines (Component Bug #423).
